lead: CVE-2025-6514, command injection in mcp-remote, JFrog, July 2025
note: A critical remote code execution flaw in a widely installed MCP client, found by researchers and fixed in 0.1.16. No exploitation of a named organisation is on the record, so there is no harm to trace to a missing control. A vulnerability with no incident is what the register calls a hazard, and hazards are only admitted when the organisation confirms a near miss.

lead: CVE-2025-59536, Claude Code SessionStart hook runs before the trust prompt, Check Point, 2026
note: A malicious repository could run commands before Claude Code showed its trust dialog. Disclosed by researchers and fixed. No named organisation reports harm from it.

lead: CVE-2026-22708, Cursor allowlist bypass through shell built-ins, Pillar Security, 2026
note: Shell built-ins such as export ran in Auto-Run allowlist mode without approval, which let injected content poison the environment of commands the user had approved. Fixed in Cursor 2.3. Researcher disclosure with no reported harm to a named organisation.

lead: Mini Shai-Hulud npm worm, persistence through .claude/settings.json, May 2026
note: The closest call so far. The worm compromised packages belonging to TanStack, Mistral AI, Guardrails AI, UiPath and others, and it wrote a SessionStart hook into Claude Code's settings file so the stealer re-ran whenever a developer opened the project. That makes an agent's config file an autostart location, which is the role a shell profile plays, and it spread through package installs rather than through anything the agent chose to do. No agent call, send or data change is in the record, so the harm does not trace to an agent control. Worth revisiting if a version is documented where the agent itself carried the action.

lead: postmark-mcp, a counterfeit email tool on npm that copied every message an agent sent, September 2025
note: Admitted on 11 October 2026 and withdrawn the same day on review. The agent did send the mail, so test 1 is met, and the evidence is strong. Test 3 is not met. Postmark published a statement establishing that the package was not theirs and that they had no involvement, so the control that failed was not Postmark's. The registry distributed it, but nothing on the record documents a control failure at the registry and it published no account of its own. The roughly three hundred organisations said to have installed it are not named. A case needs a named organisation whose control failed, because that is what the register traces. Revisit if the registry or one of the installing organisations publishes an account.

lead: Amazon Q Developer VS Code extension shipped with a data-wiping prompt, version 1.84, July 2025
note: A merged commit put an instruction into a signed official release telling the agent to clear the machine to near-factory state and delete cloud resources, and it reached roughly a million developers. AWS says the code failed to execute because of a syntax error and that no customer resources were affected, so no agent carried out the action. The harm test allows a near miss the organisation confirms, and AWS did confirm this one, but the agent-action test is separate and is not met. The missing control is real and worth the watch list on its own: nothing read the merged commit before a signed release went out.

lead: Z.ai ZCode uploaded developers' local repositories, including git history, to cloud storage, September 2026
failed_test: Pending, not rejected: evidence not yet at the bar
note: Appears to pass tests 1, 2, 3, 5 and 6. The agent packaged and sent the workspace, the code and history left the machine without disclosure or an opt-out, Z.ai is named and apologised, and the date is inside the window. Test 4 is the block. Z.ai open-sourced the client and published a long data-risk notice with it, which this register has read, but that notice documents the remediation rather than the incident, and the coverage that does describe the incident is not at the standard the evidence rule asks for. Revisit if Z.ai publishes an account of the incident itself or a reputable outlet covers it.
